What are the reasons that the gender wage gap doesn't really exist?
Simple business logic. Business are there to make money. If they can pay people 75% less to get the same exact amount of output, every business would jump at the chance to hire only women.

Yes I understand that, but I was looking for more of an explanation along the lines of why it's a fallacy and incorrect, like different life goals and past work experience for example. Not that it doesn't make sense and would result in a disproportionate amount of women in the workplace, not that I don't agree with this as a logical reason as well.

I don't think evidence actually exists that's strong enough to say it's a fallacy and incorrect but there's a lot of data that suggests it's not as pronounced as often claimed.

One argument is maternity leave. Women typically take a lot more time out of work than men for having and raising their children. This of course means women lose out on that time to gain experience and climb the ladder while men do not. If a woman has been with the company 10 years but for 2 of those was out on maternity then she's likely going to be less advanced than a man who's been with the company 10 years and only took a few months out when his kids were born.

Another argument is that for whatever reason women simply don't negotiate as hard as men do for their salaries on average. Now sexism can be brought in to this one of course but it seems to be more than only that or at least only workplace sexism. Perhaps men being the more aggressive gender in general also makes them more aggressive negotiators - if this is the case then that difference isn't due to sexism screwing women over it's due to women failing to get themselves the best possible deal.

The reality is that sexism in workplace pay probably is still a thing but it's nowhere near as bad a thing as it once was and the difference is nowhere near as bad as it's sometimes made out to be. I've worked quite a few jobs and I've never once seen any sign of workplace sexism when it comes to salary, promotions etc. etc.

Just want to expand on the maternity leave comment. There's a pretty significant percentage of women who do not go back to work after having a child. I've seen as high as 43% of women do not go return after having a child. There has to be a balance for the company to offset that risk.

I didn't think of that, thanks for responding. I've had a few annoying arguments in the last couple days
If a company is found to be systematically paying their women less without providing other benefits like maternity leave they are subject to penalties under most Western laws.

One point is that there are some jobs identified as "female" jobs, based on societal pressures or norms, that have been typically low-paying over those jobs identified as "male" jobs. For example, a "male" job like police officer, firefighter or doctor makes more than a "female" job like schoolteacher, nanny or nurse.

When compared, job to job, gender to gender, (Ex. a male CEO vs a female CEO, or male schoolteacher vs a female schoolteacher, etc.) the "wage gap" disappears into statsical meaninglessness.

It is only when you add up the pay of ALL female workers to get an average salary compared to the average salary for ALL male jobs is there a distinction.

tl;dr Pay is equal if the job is equal.
